chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, who said: I mentioned to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) the case of the istihada (inter-period bleeding) woman, so he mentioned Asma' bint Umays, and said: Indeed, Asma' gave birth to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr at al-Bayda', and in her giving birth was a blessing for the women, for those from them who give birth, or menstruate. So, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered her, and she stuffed herself (with cotton) and girded herself with a belt, and entered into ihram.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَتْ: She entered into the state of Ihram
key_terms.أَسْمَاءُ بِنْتُ عُمَيْسٍ: Asma' bint Umays, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman with istihada regarding ihram and prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal precedent for women with istihada (inter-period bleeding) to maintain their ritual purity for Hajj by following the example of Asma' bint Umays. It details the specific prophetic instructions to use istifrad (cotton packing) and a distinguishing belt (minṭaqah), highlighting the Shia scholarly view that menstruation does not invalidate the state of ihram. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh, allowing women to complete pilgrimage rites despite prolonged bleeding by distinguishing it from regular menses.
